title: The Lasting Consequence of Bernstein’s Theoretical Error
content: Julius Bernstein developed a membrane theory based on potassium diffusion and the Nernst equation, which is considered fundamental in electrochemistry. This foundational equation has been adapted for applications in biophysics and biology through the widely recognized Goldman Hodgkin Katz equation. The Nernst equation is one of the most frequently utilized equations in biology. However, a thorough comparison of their applications reveals significant similarities as well as substantial, at times irreconcilable, differences. These differences question the validity of the biological "version" of the equation, since its distinct features diverge markedly from the original Nernst equation, to the extent that the biological adaptation introduces concepts that are incompatible with current scientific understanding in the fields of thermodynamics and physics.
